plan.question: Does redistributing inverse-product-norm backward scales with the inherited half-tangent rule improve validation performance across both aligned and crossed field products under a single common source and prospectively paired seeds, or is the apparent interaction specific to seed 42 or historical source versions? The matched crossed pair improves AUC by +0.0004667050401 and unweighted Logloss by -0.0003271451568, but crossed-half remains -0.0012437529830 AUC below the aligned observer-free half anchor. The crossed-full AUC/Logloss are 0.613391730484387/0.1969854236619973; crossed-half gives 0.6138584355244538/0.1966582785051644. The historical aligned full/half corners suggest a smaller gain, but do not constitute an isolated common-source factorial. Retrieve evidence and admissible interfaces for this attribution and robustness gap before another adaptive architecture or magnitude sweep. Generic conditioning, checkpoint selection and shared-parameter adaptation remain alternatives to semantic conflict resolution; crossed products retain information.
missing_information: Authorized common-source model/config artifacts for the aligned/crossed by full/half four-cell comparison, including source/config hashes, identical initialization and data-order checks, checkpoint selection, and forward/backward boundary checks. No model or ancestor source files are exposed in this query phase; missing access is not a scientific negative.

Authorized prediction vectors and user-cluster identifiers for paired uncertainty estimates. Aggregate receipts alone cannot yield user-cluster bootstrap intervals, seed variation or significance; repeated seed-42 replays are not independent initializations.

Existing synthetic and first-512 validation checks are candidate-authored and bounded; scalar scale-moment preservation does not match optimizer updates.

Predeclared slice confirmation and missing/unseen-field coverage. Crossed-half loses AUC versus full on empty histories (8272 impressions, 310 positives), pv-absent histories and the highest user-frequency group despite improving population metrics. Empty-history changes can arise through shared learned parameters; they do not demonstrate direct history-event action.
